How to test: Ask someone to complete the main task without hints. Record the first wrong click and where they stop.
Suggested fix: Clarify the main action, label, or step order.

How to test: Move forward and back. Check the current section and whether input, filters, and scroll position return when expected.
Suggested fix: Mark the active section and preserve relevant context.

How to test: Identify the heading, primary action, and secondary actions on every key screen.
Suggested fix: Reduce competing emphasis and label the primary action clearly.

How to test: Check loading, empty, error, offline, and success states where applicable. Locate the corresponding frames in a design file.
Suggested fix: Explain the state and show the next step or retry action.

How to test: Try empty, invalid, and valid input. Check whether the user can tell which field needs attention and how to correct it.
Suggested fix: Use persistent labels and nearby error text. Associate each message with its field in the implementation.

How to test: Check deletion, cancellation, and leaving with unsaved changes where applicable.
Suggested fix: Offer undo for reversible actions. Explain consequences before irreversible actions.

How to test: Check that the same actions use consistent terms and messages explain the next step.
Suggested fix: Replace vague labels with specific verbs, such as Retry upload.

How to test: Run the journey in all supported languages. Check long strings and date, number, and price formats.
Suggested fix: Allow wrapping and flexible height. Use locale-aware formats.

How to test: On a slow connection, activate Submit several times. Check the result and retry after a timeout in a safe test environment.
Suggested fix: Show submission progress and prevent duplicates at the appropriate layer.

How to test: After the task, check that users can tell what happened and what they can do next.
Suggested fix: Show a confirmation, useful reference, or way to continue.

How to test: Review accent, surface, text, and error roles. For Material 3, check primary/on-primary and surface/on-surface across applicable themes.
Suggested fix: Use semantic color roles and measure contrast.

How to test: Compare headings, body text, labels, line wrapping, and glyph coverage for supported languages.
Suggested fix: Use a consistent type scale and test long copy.

How to test: Check alignment, visual rhythm, and spacing between related and unrelated elements.
Suggested fix: Use consistent grid and spacing values.

How to test: Check that buttons, links, switches, tabs, and dialogs match their purpose. For Material 3, compare with the component catalog.
Suggested fix: Choose the matching component and behavior. On the web, links navigate and buttons perform actions.

How to test: Review applicable default, focus, hover, pressed, selected, disabled, error, and loading states.
Suggested fix: Define the variants and their triggers. Make states distinguishable beyond color where needed.

How to test: Check text over images, dialogs, overlays, and selected states in every supported theme.
Suggested fix: Use appropriate theme tokens and stable backing surfaces for text.

How to test: Check meaning, size, and alignment. Verify accessible names for interactive icons on the working build.
Suggested fix: Label ambiguous icons and measure the hit area separately from the artwork.

How to test: Check narrow, wide, and intermediate sizes with long strings.
Suggested fix: Allow wrapping and layout changes. Remove dimensions that clip content.

How to test: Check whether transitions help explain changes. On the build, test the system reduced-motion setting.
Suggested fix: Provide a reduced or static version where appropriate.

How to test: Measure actual text and background pairs. On the web, WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for regular text and 3:1 for large text of at least 18 pt, or 14 pt bold. Check exceptions in 1.4.3.
Suggested fix: Adjust foreground, background, or backing surface and measure again.

How to test: On the web, WCAG 1.4.11 generally requires 3:1 against adjacent colors for visual information needed to identify active controls, their states, and meaningful graphics. Check exceptions.
Suggested fix: Strengthen the required border, icon, or other visual cue.

How to test: Check that users can recognize errors, selection, and status without relying on color.
Suggested fix: Add text, shape, pattern, or another distinct cue.

How to test: Use Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, arrow keys, and Escape where appropriate. Check order and keyboard traps.
Suggested fix: Use native elements and the expected keyboard pattern.

How to test: Tab through the page. Verify a visible focus indicator and check that sticky headers or banners do not fully obscure focused elements.
Suggested fix: Add a visible focus style and adjust scrolling or overlay placement.

How to test: Measure pointer targets. WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8 specifies 24 by 24 CSS pixels or an applicable exception. Verify the geometry if relying on the spacing exception.
Suggested fix: Increase the target area or separate nearby targets. Document any exception.

How to test: Test text resizing to 200%. Separately check vertically scrolling content at an equivalent width of 320 CSS pixels, with the exceptions in 1.4.10.
Suggested fix: Allow wrapping and growth. Fix clipping and unnecessary overflow.

How to test: With a screen reader, check the names, roles, values, and states of key controls.
Suggested fix: Provide programmatic labels and use native semantics or platform accessibility APIs.

How to test: Inspect heading hierarchy, landmarks, page language, and passages in a different language.
Suggested fix: Use semantic markup and appropriate lang attributes.

How to test: Check the dialog name, initial focus, and closing mechanism. On the web, check that focus stays within the modal and returns logically.
Suggested fix: Use the platform dialog pattern and repeat the keyboard and screen-reader checks.

How to test: Check text alternatives for meaningful images and captions, descriptions, or other media alternatives where applicable.
Suggested fix: Write alternatives that convey the purpose of the image or media.

How to test: Check whether a screen reader announces errors, confirmations, and updated results at the right time without duplication.
Suggested fix: Associate errors with fields and expose statuses through platform APIs.

How to test: Try completing drag or complex gesture actions with a simple pointer action where applicable.
Suggested fix: Provide an accessible alternative, such as Move up and Move down buttons.

How to test: Review looping media and movement. On the web, WCAG 2.2.2 generally requires a way to pause, stop, or hide nonessential movement that starts automatically, lasts over five seconds, and appears alongside other content.
Suggested fix: Add accessible motion controls and test reduced-motion behavior.

How to test: Where sign-in exists, test paste and password managers. Check applicable alternatives to cognitive tests under 3.3.8.
Suggested fix: Support paste and autofill. Verify the full sign-in flow and any alternative.

How to test: Test supported browsers and a real phone. Start with 320, 390, 768, and 1280 CSS pixels and include widths near layout changes.
Suggested fix: Fix overlapping content and horizontal overflow. Verify touch and keyboard navigation.

How to test: Check external links, anchors, direct URLs, refresh, Back, and an invalid route.
Suggested fix: Fix link destinations and routing. Provide a clear way out of the 404 page.

How to test: Review field results by device. Good at the 75th percentile means LCP ≤ 2.5 s, INP ≤ 200 ms, and CLS ≤ 0.1. Record lab results separately when field data is unavailable.
Suggested fix: Optimize the largest content resource, reduce long tasks, and reserve media dimensions. Measure again.

How to test: Use a slow connection and watch for shifts when images, video posters, and fonts load.
Suggested fix: Reserve dimensions, add posters, and set loading priorities based on visibility.

How to test: In a test environment, check success, server error, timeout, and retry after recovery.
Suggested fix: Explain failure, allow a retry, and retain fields that are safe to restore.

How to test: Run Lighthouse or axe on key pages and states. Separately test keyboard operation, screen-reader output, form errors, and dialogs.
Suggested fix: Confirm automated signals manually and record reproducible evidence.

How to test: Check the browser title, page language, heading, and social preview where relevant.
Suggested fix: Use a unique title, correct lang, and a consistent set of preview metadata. Verify the deployed preview.

How to test: Measure actual hit areas. Android recommends at least 48 by 48 dp. Apple HIG lists 44 by 44 pt as the default control size for iOS and iPadOS.
Suggested fix: Increase hit areas and check that neighboring targets do not overlap.

How to test: Check phones, wider windows, orientation, and multitasking where supported.
Suggested fix: Adapt layout to the current window size while preserving context. On Android, use window size classes.

How to test: Enable larger text on Android or Dynamic Type on iOS. Check menus, forms, and dialogs.
Suggested fix: Allow wrapping, container growth, and scrolling.

How to test: Complete the key journey with the platform screen reader. Check reading order, names, and state announcements.
Suggested fix: Improve labels, groups, and traversal order. Retest on a device.

How to test: Check system Back, safe areas or insets, and whether the last field and submit button remain usable when the keyboard opens.
Suggested fix: Account for system insets and allow the form to scroll.

How to test: Deny a relevant permission, then test with the network off separately. Check how the user continues or retries.
Suggested fix: Request permissions in context and explain how to proceed after refusal.

How to test: Background the app partway through the journey, then reopen it. Check state restoration and completed actions.
Suggested fix: Restore relevant state and prevent duplicate actions.

How to test: Check whether repeated elements use component instances and differences are expressed as variants or properties.
Suggested fix: Connect instances to main components and name variants by purpose.

How to test: Compare repeated color, type, and spacing values across frames.
Suggested fix: Apply consistent styles and variables. Check the relevant modes.

How to test: Resize frames and replace short labels with longer copy. Check wrapping, buttons, and nested layouts.
Suggested fix: Configure Hug, Fill, and sizing constraints to match intent.

How to test: Run the main path, Back, and an error-recovery branch.
Suggested fix: Connect the relevant frames and annotate behavior for implementation.

How to test: Check that intended accessible names, focus order, and error messages are documented.
Suggested fix: Annotate key components and verify actual behavior on the build.

How to test: Check the design version, states, responsive rules, source assets, and interaction details.
Suggested fix: Record expected behavior and compare the implementation with the agreed design.

How to test: Try a long heading, a long translation, an empty list, and a large number of cards.
Suggested fix: Save representative frames and communicate the expected behavior.

How to test: For projects using @material/web, load the production build in supported browsers. Check that every required md-* element upgrades before its first use, including deep links and routes with lazy-loaded components.
Suggested fix: Pin and record the version. Import the required components at the appropriate entry point and add a smoke test for the built page.

How to test: Verify a shared system token and a component-specific override in light and dark themes. Check the rendered states after changing the theme, including overlays and components in separately styled containers.
Suggested fix: Use documented CSS custom properties and ensure the theme scope reaches every component instance.

How to test: In a real form, exercise md-text-field and md-select with valid and invalid values. Inspect submitted entries, including names, selected values, and disabled fields. Reset and confirm the expected initial state returns.
Suggested fix: Set names and defaults, use the component's form integration, and add a regression test for submission and reset.

How to test: Trigger a missing required value, then a custom application error, then correct the value. Verify the message, submission behavior, and error clearing. An error style alone does not prove that the form blocks submission.
Suggested fix: Use the validity APIs for constraints that must prevent submission. Keep visual error state and error copy synchronized with validity.

How to test: Open an md-dialog and test its confirm and cancel actions, Escape, and scrim dismissal where enabled. Reopen after each exit and check which action or value the application handles.
Suggested fix: Assign explicit action values and handle cancel and close separately as needed. Only run the business action for an explicit confirmation.

How to test: Verify icon-only names and that a Material Web toggle's selected state and its exposed pressed state follow the real application value, including after a reset or failed update.
Suggested fix: Bind state to the same application value, use the documented accessible labeling options, and test both states with assistive technology.

How to test: Place a primary action and a secondary action inside the same form. Test clicking each, Enter in a field, and any action located outside the form that targets it by ID.
Suggested fix: Use explicit button types and form association where needed. Keep secondary actions from submitting accidentally.

Check: Custom element focus and disabled state
How to test: On an md-* button, field, or select, check keyboard focus and disabled behavior in the real page after applying framework bindings and theme overrides. Verify that a disabled action cannot execute.
Suggested fix: Use component properties and supported CSS tokens, then retest with keyboard and pointer. Avoid styling assumptions about private shadow DOM.

How to test: Inventory the Material dependencies and note which audited screens are XML Views, Compose, or mixed. Run a representative screen from each in the supported build.
Suggested fix: Record the exact versions and use the matching theme and component docs. Treat MDC Android Views as a maintained legacy stack and follow the Compose-first guidance for new Material work.

How to test: On a Views screen, compare the base activity theme with the component theme and any dialog or sheet overlays. Switch light and dark mode and inspect the same field or button.
Suggested fix: Use compatible Material theme parents and documented widget styles or overlays. Test inside the actual screen and dialog context.

How to test: For an MDC Android Views field, verify where the hint is set. Trigger and clear an error, change any end-icon state, and check the result with TalkBack.
Suggested fix: Set the hint on TextInputLayout, keep helper and error text in sync, and verify the end icon has a meaningful accessible description.

How to test: Test a legacy MDC bottom sheet in its supported collapsed and expanded states. If it uses BottomSheetDragHandleView, verify the accessibility actions and dismissal without requiring a drag gesture.
Suggested fix: Use the documented drag handle or another accessible control and provide a clear dismissal path where appropriate.

How to test: In the real bottom sheet or Compose screen, open the IME and scroll to the last action. Repeat with gesture navigation and verify status-bar and navigation-bar areas.
Suggested fix: Use the appropriate edge-to-edge and inset APIs. Check for double padding and controls hidden by system UI.

How to test: When dynamic color is supported by the app, run it with different system palettes and compare it with the app fallback on an unsupported or disabled configuration. Check meaningful color pairs in both themes.
Suggested fix: Provide explicit light and dark fallback schemes and use paired color roles for content and surfaces.

How to test: Inspect the semantics of a custom composable with an icon, text, and a state. Use TalkBack to check whether it exposes one coherent control and the intended action and state.
Suggested fix: Use Material composables or appropriate Compose semantics. Merge only where the child content belongs to one control.

How to test: On a Compose build, run automated accessibility checks on a representative user journey and verify that the relevant actions actually trigger checks. Repeat key states with TalkBack.
Suggested fix: Enable supported Compose accessibility testing in the instrumented test suite and keep a manual device pass.

How to test: Identify the Material iOS components still in the app and record their exact versions, ownership, and flows. Verify a representative flow on supported iOS versions.
Suggested fix: Keep a regression list for existing MDC iOS screens and plan replacements using SwiftUI or UIKit where appropriate.

How to test: With VoiceOver, move to a legacy Material text field before input, after input, and after validation fails. Listen for the floating label, value, and assistive or error text. Repeat for any custom label override.
Suggested fix: Preserve the necessary label, value, and error information without repetition. Verify any explicit accessibility label with VoiceOver.

How to test: In legacy filled or outlined text fields and text areas, test long floating and assistive labels at large text sizes. Check the actual Auto Layout or manual sizing behavior.
Suggested fix: Allow the field to use its intrinsic or measured height, and remove fixed heights that clip labels or errors.

How to test: Test legacy Material typography or custom fonts at standard and accessibility text sizes. Check headings, labels, buttons, and error text for correct scaling.
Suggested fix: Use Dynamic Type-aware typography. In SwiftUI, choose the appropriate relative text style and scale layout values where needed.

How to test: Replace or test a mapped native control in a migration build. Compare VoiceOver labels, traits, values, and actions with the intended behavior, and inspect the resulting element tree.
Suggested fix: Prefer native control semantics. Add labels, values, or traits only where needed and verify with Accessibility Inspector and VoiceOver.

How to test: With system Reduce Motion enabled, run the original and replacement transitions for a legacy Material flow. Check that completion and state remain understandable.
Suggested fix: Use a reduced transition, such as a simple fade where appropriate, and honor the system preference through the platform APIs.

How to test: Open a clean session at a narrow width with storage preferences unset. Check whether the banner covers the main action, whether its controls work with keyboard input, and whether the underlying task resumes after dismissal.
Suggested fix: Keep the main task visible when possible. Match the overlay's interaction and focus behavior to whether it is modal.

How to test: Select a meaningful filter, open a detail page, then use Back and Forward. Refresh or open the filtered URL in a fresh tab if the filter is meant to be shareable.
Suggested fix: Encode shareable state in the URL and restore it from navigation. Preserve transient UI state only where the journey calls for it.

How to test: With the keyboard, activate a route-changing link. Check the document title, focus position, and next Tab stop. Repeat when returning to a list and check that focus and scroll return to a useful location.
Suggested fix: Define focus behavior for route transitions. Use a meaningful heading or main region as a destination when appropriate, and restore the trigger on return when it still exists.

How to test: Inspect the server-delivered head and the rendered head for the same public route. Compare og:title, og:description, og:image and og:url with the actual project. Check that the preview image loads without a session.
Suggested fix: Generate one intended value for each singleton tag and remove conflicting defaults. Use absolute, publicly accessible image URLs.

Check: Real HTTP status for a missing route
How to test: Request an invalid public URL directly and check the HTTP status as well as the visible error page. Check that the recovery link works.
Suggested fix: Return an appropriate 404 or 410 for permanently missing content and render the recovery page with that status.

How to test: For languages intended to appear separately in search, open each published locale URL directly in a fresh session. Check the initial language, self or intended canonical URL, and reciprocal hreflang links.
Suggested fix: Use stable locale URLs with matching content and consistent canonical and alternate declarations. Mark this check not applicable if the project has no separate indexable language URLs.

How to test: With a cold cache, compare the downloaded image URLs and sizes on narrow and wide screens. Locate the measured LCP element. Check that responsive selection matches layout and that a visible LCP image is not lazy-loaded.
Suggested fix: Use width-appropriate assets with srcset and sizes where suitable. Reserve image dimensions and prioritize the measured LCP image when appropriate.

How to test: Exercise a Copy action when clipboard writing fails or is denied. Confirm that the page does not announce success and the user can still select and copy the content.
Suggested fix: Handle the rejected write and offer a selectable text fallback. Announce success only after the write succeeds.

How to test: If a carousel rotates automatically, move keyboard focus into it and hover over it. Check the stop control, that it does not resume after focus enters unless the user restarts it, and that slide changes do not displace the active task.
Suggested fix: Follow the carousel pattern for rotation controls, focus, and announcements. Keep manual navigation available.

How to test: Enable system reduced motion before opening a web build. Check CSS transitions, JavaScript animation, canvas or decorative media if used. Navigate to another route and retest.
Suggested fix: Apply the preference wherever motion is generated. Use stable static or reduced states and preserve task feedback.

How to test: On Android, interrupt the journey and reproduce activity or process recreation in a test build. Verify the selected item, position, or safe-to-restore draft and check that completed actions do not repeat.
Suggested fix: Save minimal restorable UI state and reload durable data from its owner. Combine local state tests with an app-level recreation test.

How to test: On a screen with adaptive list-detail navigation, select an item and resize the app between single and dual panes. Check the selected item and Back behavior at each size.
Suggested fix: Keep selection and navigation state consistent across pane changes. Define what Back should do in each layout.

Check: Verified deep links and web fallback
How to test: For a feature with Android App Links or iOS universal links, open a documented URL with the app installed and again without it. Test the intended detail screen and a safe fallback for invalid or unauthorized destinations.
Suggested fix: Validate app and domain association. Route supported links to the intended screen and keep a usable browser destination.

Check: iOS accessibility audit in UI tests
How to test: In an iOS UI test on a supported test target, run the accessibility audit after navigating to key states such as form errors and modal screens. Confirm and triage findings and repeat the important flows with VoiceOver.
Suggested fix: Add screen-specific audit steps and document any narrowly scoped exceptions. Keep manual device testing.

Check: Token mapping from design to build
How to test: Pick representative semantic tokens and compare the Figma variable and mode with the implemented token name and value in the same theme. Repeat on a nested component.
Suggested fix: Document the design-to-code mapping and resolve conflicting aliases or overrides.

How to test: Open the handoff as a developer. Find the approved frame, its linked assets, and changes since the previous delivery. Where Dev Mode is available, check the relevant ready-for-dev status and changed frames.
Suggested fix: Use a single approved entry point, visible revision notes, and the applicable handoff status.

Check: Interaction details for a custom component
How to test: Ask a reviewer to implement a custom control from the handoff alone. Check whether states, focus order, accessible name, keyboard actions, and failure behavior are specified for the target platform.
Suggested fix: Add missing interaction details to the approved component and link the testable prototype state.

Check: Prototype starts from a clean state
How to test: Open each shared flow in a fresh viewer session. Verify the starting frame, default variable mode, branch behavior, and expected reset or restart. Repeat in a different flow.
Suggested fix: Set explicit flow starts, confirm shared links, and reset or initialize prototype variables where the experience requires it.
